svg.aria-label: NB-IoT broadcast schedule: SIB1-NB and SI windows
svg.title: NB-IoT broadcast schedule: SIB1-NB and SI windows
svg.text: When does cell 260 say what? The broadcast timetable I had to follow
SIB1-NB over one 2.56 s cycle (256 frames): subframe 4 of every even frame, 16 repetitions of 8 subframes
Each numbered block is one full copy (frames 0, 2, 4 … 14 → 8 subframes). A meter in a deep basement adds up to 16 copies;
I needed one: the CRC passed on the first copy every time, so my log says "1 repetition combined".
SI-message 1 (SIB2 + SIB3): one 960 ms window every 512 frames, starting at frame 12
nothing for this SI message until frame 524 (= 512 + 12)
Violet ticks = a new transmission every 4th frame (every4thRF). I decoded the ones starting at SFN 12, 16 and 524.
Zoom: one transmission needs 8 free subframes. Starting at SFN 12 they fall here
SI-message 1, subframe number 1…8 of the codeword
taken: NPBCH, NPSS, SIB1 (even frames), NSSS (even frames)
The tower never says "the SI message starts now". The rules are in 3GPP TS 36.331 and 36.213, and the numbers come from SIB1:
si-Periodicity rf512, si-RadioFrameOffset 12, si-WindowLength ms960, si-RepetitionPattern every4thRF, si-TB b328 (→ 8 subframes).
My decoder recomputes this table for every frame, collects exactly those 8 subframes, and only then tries to decode.
One missed or extra subframe and the CRC fails. Every SI decode in my log passed on the first transmission.
This is also why the decoder needs H-SFN: the SI timetable is counted in absolute frames (H-SFN × 1024 + SFN).
